Looking at the image, I can observe:

**Affected part:** Leaf surface

**Key visual features:**
- Green leaf with white/gray powdery patches on the leaf surface
- The powdery coating appears to be spreading across the leaf in irregular patches
- The underlying leaf tissue remains green but with the whitish powdery growth overlaying it
- No distinct brown necrotic lesions with concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight, Target Spot)
- No water-soaked oily blotches (ruling out Late Blight)
- No small dark-centered circular spots (ruling out Septoria)

**Analysis:**
The dominant feature is a white, powdery coating on the leaf surface. This matches the Powdery Mildew description: *"White, powdery sporulation on both the tops and undersides of leaves, in round spots that begin small but expand and converge."* The leaf appears to still be attached and retains its green color underneath the powdery growth, which also fits the description of leaves withering but remaining attached. The white powdery texture is distinctive and doesn't resemble the cottony sporulation of Late Blight (which would require purple-brown lesions) or the olive/brown velvety mold of Leaf Mold.
